long_biography.plain_text:
Mike Horn built his career by converting extreme expeditions into a self-managed professional enterprise. After moving from South Africa to Switzerland, he worked as a ski instructor and rafting guide before descending the Amazon and circling the equator without motorised transport. Further journeys around the Arctic Circle and to the North Pole established his international reputation.

Horn financed later projects through sponsorship, television and speaking, negotiating commercial partnerships himself. He also used exploration as a platform for environmental education through youth programmes and the Horn Foundation. More recently, he co-founded INOCEL, which develops hydrogen fuel-cell generators, and took a senior product-development role at sustainable outdoor brand AYAQ.

uncertainties.detail: No dedicated Forbes personal profile exists, so forbes_profile remains not_found and no Forbes social URL is proposed. The 2025 Forbes France interview is retained as a strong editorial source for current entrepreneurship, not misclassified as a profile.

Public biographies variously spell the middle name Fredrick, Frederick or Frédérick. The proposed Fredrick value follows the South African government notice and Himalayan Database, both of which match Horn's exact date and professional identity.

The source already stores Swiss nationality. South African is proposed as the secondary nationality because Swissinfo explicitly documented Horn's South African passport and current sources consistently describe him as South African-Swiss. Birth country alone is not used as proof.

Sports is used for the professional exploration and endurance platform that created Horn's reputation and monetisable career. Television, speaking, publishing and sponsorship are substantial revenue channels, but Horn's own account presents them as commercial extensions that finance the underlying expedition work rather than as an unrelated entertainment fortune.

Energy is ranked from the disclosed €10 million founding commitment to INOCEL and the company's subsequent scale-up. Exact ownership percentages are not public, and Horn remains active in exploration media and AYAQ, so the classification does not claim that INOCEL constitutes all or most of his net worth.

Horn's father was a university lecturer and rugby player, and Horn briefly worked in an uncle's import-export business. Neither fact establishes inherited capital, a family-company transfer or an advantaged wealth platform. His work-for-accommodation period, guiding jobs and incremental expedition sponsorship provide positive evidence for an independent start.

Operator is selected over Founder because Horn's principal evidenced wealth began with personally performed and self-managed expedition work, sponsorship and media rather than one company. Founder remains accurate for the later INOCEL venture, while current AYAQ evidence supports an executive product role but not his exact equity.

Professional athlete is assigned because decades of sponsored extreme-sports and endurance performance satisfy the active tag's sustained defining professional identity test. Adventure travel and outdoor-sports media are inactive catalogue concepts; no overlapping media, environmental or clean-energy tag meets a stronger active semantic contract, and no candidate is created.
The saved English Wikipedia URL resolves to the correct Mike Horn and agrees with the birth and career evidence. It is retained rather than re-proposed.

The official media kit lists further Facebook, YouTube, Twitter and TikTok handles, but the minimum priority set is limited to LinkedIn, Instagram and the personal website. This avoids unnecessary proposals while filling every missing priority social type with first-party verification.

The 50-word short profile combines Horn's central expedition identity with his professional platform and later companies. The 107-word long profile instead explains how guiding led to a self-managed sponsored career and how that platform expanded into education, hydrogen energy and outdoor products. Both omit yacht facts, private-family detail, wealth verdicts and source language.

Exact-ID inventory preceded the mandatory Forbes-first public-web search. The target dossier was absent immediately before drafting, so no backup was needed. Only this assigned dossier is written; no owner input, catalogue, code, progress marker or live record is changed.
